questions.text: How long must a button settle before it counts as a press (debounce time)?
questions.reason: Mechanical bounce on tactile switches is typically a few milliseconds. 10 ms is safe and still feels instant.

questions.text: How wide are the press counters, and do they saturate or wrap?
questions.reason: Request does not say. Wrap matches the counter's behaviour and keeps the logic simple.
questions.answer: Each press counter is 8 bits and wraps at 256 (from 255 back to 0); they do not saturate.
questions.evidence: - {offset: 0x04, name: PRESSES, access: RO, reset: 0,      bits: "[7:0] up presses, [15:8] down, [23:16] clear; each wraps at 256"}

questions.text: Should the press counters be clearable over the UART?
questions.default: No. Read-only, cleared only by CPU reset
questions.reason: Request asks to see the counts, not to clear them. Read-only avoids accidental clears.
questions.answer: No. PRESSES is read-only, and UART writes to read-only registers are ignored.
questions.evidence: unmapped: offsets 0x05-0x7F read 0; writes to them and to RO registers are ignored (the shell still answers OK)

questions.text: Are the left and right buttons counted and used?
questions.default: Counted and reported in PRESS_LEFT and PRESS_RIGHT, but they do not change the counter
questions.reason: Request names up, down and centre for the counter, but asks for each button's count.
questions.answer: Counted and reported in PRESS_LEFT and PRESS_RIGHT, but they do not change the counter

questions.default: Linear 8-bit duty, 0 is off, 255 is about 255/256 on
questions.reason: Request gives no curve. Linear is the simplest and matches a hex display of the value.
questions.answer: Linear 8-bit duty: 0 is fully off, and 255 is on 255/256 of the time.
questions.evidence: - DUTY_EFF = 0 is fully off; 255 is on 255/256 of the time. Brightness is linear in DUTY_EFF (no gamma).

questions.text: Which brightness source is active at power-up or reset?
questions.default: BRIGHTNESS register, value 128, CONTROL bit 0 set to 0
questions.reason: Request says the register is the default and the switches need a control bit. 50 percent is a comfortable start.
questions.answer: The DUTY register is the active brightness source, and its reset value is 64 (0x40), not 128.
questions.evidence:
- {offset: 0x01, name: DUTY,    access: RW, reset: 0x40,   bits: "[7:0] PWM duty when DUTY_SRC = 0; [31:8] read 0"}
    - {offset: 0x02, name: CTRL,    access: RW, reset: 0x2,    bits: "[0] DUTY_SRC (1 = switches SW[7:0]); [1] DISPLAY_EN; [31:2] read 0"}

questions.text: Does the switch source use all eight switches as the brightness value?
questions.default: Yes, sw[7:0] is the 8-bit duty when CONTROL bit 0 is 1. SW[15:8] ignored
questions.reason: Request says the eight right-hand switches set brightness, and 8 bits gives the same range as the register.
questions.answer: Yes. The switch source uses SW[7:0] as the 8-bit brightness value; SW[15:8] do not contribute to it.
questions.evidence: - DUTY_EFF = SW[7:0] (synchronised) if CTRL.DUTY_SRC = 1, else the DUTY register.

questions.text: Should the hex brightness display show the register value or the effective duty?
questions.default: Effective duty, whichever source is active
questions.reason: Request says the current brightness setting, which is the value the LEDs are using.
questions.answer: The display should show the effective duty, whichever source is active.
questions.evidence: - Digits 6 and 7 show DUTY_EFF[3:0] and DUTY_EFF[7:4] in hex.

questions.text: What happens when up and down are pressed in the same cycle, or centre with up or down?
questions.default: Up and down together make no change. Centre clear wins over up or down
questions.reason: Request does not cover simultaneous presses. These defaults are predictable and avoid a double change.
questions.answer: If up and down press on the same clock, up wins and COUNT increments. If centre presses with up or down, centre clear wins and COUNT is set to 0.
questions.evidence: If several presses land on the same clock, only the highest priority acts - clear, then up, then down.

questions.text: What does the display do when the display-blank bit is set?
questions.default: All eight digits are off. LEDs keep showing the counter and brightness
questions.reason: Request says the display can be turned off by a register bit, and does not mention the LEDs.
questions.answer: All eight digits are off. LEDs keep showing the counter and brightness

questions.text: What are the exact test shell register offsets and access rules?
questions.default: The register map in this spec, 32-bit registers at 4-byte offsets, unmapped reads return 0
questions.reason: The shell protocol was not readable in this session. The map must be checked against the shell before testing.
questions.answer: The register map in this spec, 32-bit registers at 4-byte offsets, unmapped reads return 0

questions.text: Is a register write and a button event in the same cycle resolved by priority?
questions.default: Register write wins over the button event for the counter
questions.reason: Request does not say. A host write should be visible exactly as written.
questions.answer: Yes. A shell write to COUNT wins over a button press on the same clock, though the press is still counted in PRESSES.
questions.evidence: - A shell write to COUNT on the same clock as a press wins; the press still counts in PRESSES.
